claims.text: Hastelloy C-276 is a nickel-based high-temperature alloy.
Hastelloy C-276 has high strength and high toughness.
NMQL uses solid nanoparticles added to an MQL base fluid.
The proposed NMQL micro-grinding process uses a high-pressure air stream and micron-sized cutting-fluid droplets.
Nano-lubricant particles have high heat-transfer coefficients and friction-reduction properties.
Adding nanoparticles improves the cooling and lubrication characteristics of the base fluid.
NMQL reduces friction at the tool-workpiece contact area.
NMQL reduces heat transfer in the tool-workpiece contact area.
During micro-grinding of Hastelloy C-276, NMQL will reduce surface roughness relative to dry grinding or conventional MQL.
During micro-grinding of Hastelloy C-276, NMQL will reduce cutting temperature relative to dry grinding or conventional MQL.
During micro-grinding of Hastelloy C-276, NMQL will reduce tool wear relative to dry grinding or conventional MQL.
During micro-grinding of Hastelloy C-276, NMQL will improve surface quality relative to dry grinding or conventional MQL.
During micro-grinding of Hastelloy C-276, NMQL will improve surface microhardness relative to dry grinding or conventional MQL.
NMQL containing 0.05% h-BN has reduced cutting force, cutting temperature, and surface roughness in AISI 1045 machining.
NMQL has improved surface quality and reduced tool wear during turning of Inconel 718 compared with dry and MQL conditions.
Hastelloy C-276 retains useful wear and corrosion resistance in harsh chemical and high-temperature environments.
The surface improvements produced by NMQL will remain effective during service in aggressive high-temperature and harsh chemical environments.
The optimum nanoparticle type and concentration, and the applicability of NMQL across different high-temperature alloys, remain uncertain.
Failure of NMQL to significantly improve the measured surface and mechanical characteristics over both MQL and dry grinding would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says NMQL reduces heat transfer at the contact, whereas the mediator and mechanism invoke high heat-transfer coefficients and improved heat transfer/cooling. The intended claim may be reduced heat accumulation or reduced workpiece temperature, but that distinction is not stated.
